_comment: Single source of truth for the Omega brand gate (OMEGA-DELTA-0017,
OMEGA-DELTA-0018 and OMEGA-DELTA-0022). Read by crates/omega_deltas on the
source tree and by script/verify-omega-brand on the packaged application,
so the two sides cannot drift apart on what counts as a competitor's name.
Do not add an entry to third_party_allowances to make a build pass. An
allowance means the asset identifies somebody else's product the way
ai_anthropic.svg identifies Anthropic, not that Omega presents itself as
that product.
Read the scoping note on OMEGA-DELTA-0022 before adding a section. Three
times running, a gate scoped to a directory or a list reported green about
that directory and said nothing about the product: rc6 scanned the binary
for three identity literals, rc10 added assets/icons and the packaged
Info.plist, and rc11 still shipped Zed artwork out of assets/images and a
user-facing 'zed:' command namespace, because neither was in any list. A
new section belongs here only if its inventory is derived from the thing
that decides what ships.
words are matched case-sensitively at ASCII alphanumeric boundaries, so
'Zed' and "Zed's" match while 'Zedd' does not.
Lowercase 'zed' used to be excluded here, and the reason written down was
that it is a substring of 'authorized', 'organized' and 'normalized'. That
reason was wrong: the boundary rule already excludes all three, because
the 'zed' in 'authorized' has an 'i' before it. The exclusion cost nothing
it claimed to save and hid the rendered --help of both shipped binaries --
'Run zed in the foreground', 'Run zed in dev-server mode', 'Instructs zed
to run as a dev server' -- through 0.2.0-rc14 (omega#89).
It is in now. Measured on this tree, the lowercase hits are dominated by
identifiers -- zed_actions, zed::, .zed/, zed://, ZED_* -- and is_prose()
drops those, because a token is not a sentence. What survives the prose
filter is copy, and copy is what this gate is for. An inherited identifier
that does reach a sentence is classified as fork_seam with the reason,
not filtered away silently.
OMEGA-DELTA-0024. The admitted first-party agent identity, and the
phrasings that would present somebody else's as ours.
phrases are matched case-insensitively as substrings, because the leak
that shipped in 0.2.0-rc10 was not a variant of a checked string, it was
a neighbour of one. A gate that knows exactly one literal finds exactly
one literal: 'Zed Agent' was checked and clean while 'Zed's agent' sat
in a rendered Label in three provider settings pages.
symbols forbids the identifier as well as the value it holds. Renaming
only the string leaves the next upstream rebase an obvious symbol to
restore the old identity under, which is the lesson the icon rename
already paid for.
An allowance is not an exemption for our own copy. It means the text
names Zed's product or Zed's history, the way ai_zed.svg labels Zed's
own keymap preset and model provider. Do not add one to make a build
pass.
_forbidden_path_stems_comment: A file name is a surface too. The docs page moved from zed-agent.md to
omega-agent.md, and a content scan cannot see the difference — the
renamed file says 'Omega Agent' either way. Falsifying this delta found
exactly that hole: restoring the old file name passed every check.
Matched against the file stem, case-insensitively, so it does not fire
on crates/omega or on a directory named zed_eval.

_comment: Every file in fragment_dir is merged into the packaged Info.plist by
cargo-bundle (osx_info_plist_exts = ['resources/info/*'] in
crates/omega/Cargo.toml), so the whole directory is scanned rather than a
list of known files. macOS renders NS*UsageDescription values inside its
own system permission dialogs, so a competitor's name here is presented
by the operating system, under our Developer ID signature.
assets/icons and the IconName enum are a bijection, enforced by
crates/icons test_all_icons_exist and test_no_dangling_icons, so
scanning both is a complete inventory of every icon that can ship.
This section is OMEGA-DELTA-0018 and is now a special case of
OMEGA-DELTA-0022 below, which scans every file under assets/ and every
enum that names one. It is kept because the icon set is where the marks
are pinned and because a narrower failure message is easier to act on.
reviewed_marks pins the bytes of the Omega artwork. The name rules
cannot see a logo; the digests can. Changing one of these files is a
deliberate artwork change and has to update this pin in the same commit.

third_party_allowances.ai_zed: Identifies the Zed editor's base-keymap preset (next to VS Code, JetBrains and Sublime Text) and Zed's own hosted model provider, exactly as ai_anthropic.svg identifies Anthropic. Naming somebody else's product is not Omega presenting itself as that product.

_comment: OMEGA-DELTA-0022. Every file rust-embed can ship: the asset tree plus every
directory any #[folder = ...] in the repository points at. Not a list of
asset directories -- rust-embed ships whole directories, so the directories
it names are the inventory, and a list of the ones somebody remembered is
how assets/images/zed_logo.svg and zed_x_copilot.svg reached a signed,
notarized 0.2.0-rc11 while OMEGA-DELTA-0018 reported assets/icons/ clean,
truthfully.
The roots are derived from the embed declarations rather than written here,
so a rust-embed folder added tomorrow is inside the gate the day it is
added instead of being outside it until somebody notices. If the discovery
finds no declarations at all, the gate fails rather than passing over an
empty inventory.

third_party_allowances.assets/icons/ai_zed.svg: Identifies the Zed editor's base-keymap preset (next to VS Code, JetBrains and Sublime Text) and Zed's own hosted model provider, exactly as ai_anthropic.svg identifies Anthropic. Naming somebody else's product is not Omega presenting itself as that product.

_comment: OMEGA-DELTA-0022. The enums that turn a Rust identifier into an embedded
asset path are discovered from the source, not listed here.
OMEGA-DELTA-0018 named crates/icons/src/icons.rs in this file. VectorName
in crates/ui/src/components/image.rs does exactly the same job for
assets/images/ and was outside the gate, so VectorName::ZedLogo and
VectorName::ZedXCopilot survived rc11. Any enum whose impl builds an
asset path with format!("<dir>/{...}") is found the same way, whichever
crate it is added to.
required_discoveries is the anti-vacuity guard: if the discovery stops
finding these, the parser broke and the check is reporting green about
nothing.

third_party_allowances.IconName::AiZed: Renders assets/icons/ai_zed.svg, allowed above for the same reason.

_comment: OMEGA-DELTA-0022. Every gpui action in the repository, because the
command palette shows 'namespace: action name' for all of them and there
are exactly two ways to declare one: actions!(namespace, [...]) and
#[action(namespace = ...)] on a derive. Scanning both over the whole
crates tree is the complete set of labels the palette can display.
rc11's palette offered 'zed: about', 'zed: quit' and 'zed: get merch'
while the compatibility allow-list recorded the zed namespace as 'not
user-facing product copy'. The targets were already correct; the label
was the defect. Nothing had ever read an action declaration.
deprecated_aliases are exempt: an alias exists to name the OLD action so
an existing user keymap keeps resolving, and is never shown in the
palette.
OMEGA-DELTA-0031. Every brand-bearing prose literal that can reach a user,
derived from what ships and classified one by one.
OMEGA-DELTA-0022 closed assets, asset-name enums and command-palette labels
with derived inventories. Prose was the hole it named and could not close:
the string half enforced the compatibility allow-list's `blocked` claims,
which is a written-down denylist, so a NEW sentence naming Zed as the
product passed until somebody remembered to add it. That is exactly how
'Use GitHub Copilot in Zed' shipped in 0.2.0-rc11, and the signed,
notarized 0.2.0-rc13 still told the user 'Click Connect below to start
using Ollama in Zed'.
This section inverts the default. The inventory is derived; every literal
in it must be CLASSIFIED here; anything unclassified fails. A new sentence
is unclassified the moment it is written, so it fails on the commit that
adds it rather than on the release that ships it.
THE RULE, for telling a product claim from a third-party reference:
substitute our own name. If the sentence stays TRUE with 'Omega' in place
of the brand, the brand was standing where our product's name belongs and
it is a product claim -- rewrite it. 'start using Ollama in Zed' becomes
'start using Ollama in Omega', which is true, so it was a claim about us.
If the substitution makes the sentence FALSE, it states a fact about
somebody else's product, service, documentation, or authorship -- keep it.
'similar to Zed's default keybindings' does not become true of Omega's
keybindings, so the preset is really describing Zed. Classes below are
the reasons a substitution would have been false.
Do not add an entry to make a build pass. An entry is a written record
that somebody read the sentence and decided it names Zed rather than us.

classes.zed_product: Names Zed's own editor, keymap preset, or documentation.
classes.zed_service: Names Zed's hosted service, account, plan, billing, server, or cloud artifact.
classes.zed_authorship: Records Zed as the author or copyright holder of an inherited artifact.
classes.fork_seam: Names an inherited identifier -- a font family, a marker string -- where the value IS the thing being named, so renaming it breaks a lookup rather than a claim.
classes.omega_contrast: Omega-authored copy that names Zed in order to say how Omega differs from it.

_derivation_comment: Four streams, each derived from a mechanism that exists in the tree rather
than from a list of files somebody remembered:
rust_string  every Rust string literal under rust_root, including raw and
multi-line ones, outside #[cfg(test)] items and test files.
A literal is compiled in; nothing can prove one is never
rendered, and assuming so is what left the provider copy
standing through four release candidates.
schema_doc   doc comments in a file that really derives JsonSchema, which
is how schemars turns them into the settings schema's
`description` values and how the settings editor renders
them as tooltips. Doc lines are stripped before the derive is
looked for, so a derive inside a doc EXAMPLE does not pull a
whole framework crate's rustdoc into the inventory.
action_doc   doc comments inside an actions!(...) body or immediately
above an #[action(...)] derive -- the action descriptions the
keymap editor shows.
clap_doc     doc comments in a file deriving Parser/Args/Subcommand or
using #[command(...)], which clap prints as --help output.
asset        every line of every text file in the embedded-asset
inventory OMEGA-DELTA-0022 already derives -- keymap and
default-settings comments, agent prompt templates, themes.
A literal is in the inventory when it carries a brand.words / brand.substrings
hit AND is prose-shaped: at least three whitespace-separated tokens, at least
two of them plain alphabetic words. That keeps identifiers, paths and headers
out, and it is the one judgement in the derivation -- widen it before
narrowing it.
_guard_comment: The floors are on what the scanners READ, not on what they find, because a
clean tree finds little and a broken parser finds nothing, and those two
must not look the same. Every classified entry is also asserted to still be
present, so the registry cannot become a graveyard and a scanner that stops
reading a stream fails on that stream's entries.

_comment: OMEGA-DELTA-0038. What the packaged half opens, and how much of it.
Until omega#89 every packaged check in script/verify-omega-brand opened
Contents/MacOS/omega and nothing else, while script/bundle-omega-rc copied
and signed `cli` and `omega-identity-proof` into the same directory. That
is why `cli` shipped an uninstaller that deleted a competitor's editor and
no Omega path at all through two published prereleases, under a green gate
(omega#88): the defect was never inside a file any check opened.
The executable inventory is now derived by walking the bundle for Mach-O
magic, so a helper added tomorrow is inside the gate the day it is added.
The floors are on what the scans READ, not on what they find.
minimum_rendered_invocations is the guard on the rendered-help scan: it
runs the shipped binaries with --help and --version and reads what comes
back, because clap builds the sentence a person sees at run time out of
doc lines the source scan only ever sees separately.
OMEGA-DELTA-0203 raised minimum_executables from 3 to 4: the bundle now
ships the first-party `scv` agent beside `omega`, `cli` and
`omega-identity-proof`, and a floor below what ships is the shape
omega#88 shipped in.
